lines.text: How can your smartphone instantly unlock using your face, even when you're sitting in pitch-black darkness?
It doesn't use a normal visual selfie camera.
Hidden in the notch is a flood illuminator and a microscopic vertical-cavity laser called a dot projector.
The dot projector beams thirty thousand invisible infrared light dots directly onto your face.
An infrared camera reads the reflected dot grid, capturing a precise three-dimensional mathematical contour of your face.
A dedicated neural engine compares this depth map against enrolled biometric templates in under a tenth of a second.
Because it reads true geometric depth with invisible infrared, photos or sleeping eyes can never unlock it.
